correctness.rationale: The equilibrium-age identity, geometric sum and density-matrix purity normalization reconstruct the exact reduced functional |1-E[i^L]|^2/(4 mu^2). For 1<=mu<=3/2, the pointwise linear support inequality yields the sharp lower certificate 1+(2-mu)^2, with equality only at lengths 1,3. For 3/2<=mu<=4, a second linear support inequality yields (4-mu)^2/5, with equality on 1,3,4 and unique weights. For mu>=4 complete dephasing is exactly support on positive multiples of four. For 1<=mu<=2, a sharp vector and first-moment bound yields upper 2+2(mu-1)^2; above 2 a triangle bound yields four, exactly for lengths congruent to two modulo four. Fixed-mean interpolation fills the entire closed interval. Critical equality cases and boundaries are shown analytically. A standalone exact-rational checker passed 69,251 finite diagnostic assertion groups and is not treated as proof of infinite cases.

value.rationale: For the canonical one-qubit Clifford quarter-turn gate, optimization over every independent positive-integer renewal clock at fixed expected interval produces a full sharp purity range, all extremizing protocols, and three mathematically distinct support/dephasing transitions. The clock discretization is physically motivated by gate sequences and changes the answer qualitatively relative to real-time renewal resetting. The exact constraints clarify when complete dephasing can occur and how clock regularity limits coherence; ideal-gate and initialization restrictions are explicitly acknowledged. Not a trivial isolated parameter computation.
